answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, with rewards released only after independent agents verify the result. Creating a thousand aliases then does not create a thousand free votes: each must tie up capital, and provably fraudulent submissions lose their stake. A delta in the admission threshold can tune security against participation costs; velvet and lagoon are merely labels, not extra identities or trust. The attacker pays in capital, verification effort, and forfeited stake.
